title: Person Bowing Emoji 🙇 Meaning: Sorry, Thanks or Please
description: 🙇 is a deep Japanese bow for a sincere apology, heartfelt thanks or a big favor. Many people misread it as a push-up or a nap. Here is what it really shows.
summary: 🙇 shows a person bowing deeply, head lowered toward the ground. It comes from Japanese etiquette, where a deep bow expresses sincere apology, profound gratitude or a humble request. Online it means “I’m so sorry,” “thank you so much,” or “please, I’m begging you,” and sometimes exaggerated admiration.
meaning: The posture in this emoji is a formal bow, and in its deepest form it resembles dogeza, the Japanese act of kneeling with head and hands to the floor. That gesture is reserved for serious apologies and earnest pleas. Unicode originally named the emoji “Person Bowing Deeply,” and in Japanese messaging it accompanies phrases for “I’m sorry” and “please treat me kindly.”

Outside Japan, the picture confuses people. With only a head and shoulders above a flat line, it has been read as someone doing a push-up, lying down for a massage, resting their head on a desk, or peeking over a table. Those readings produced real secondary uses: you will see 🙇 in posts about being exhausted, bored in class or face-down with stress.

Among people who know what it depicts, the emoji is the strongest way to apologize or give thanks in a single character. “I completely forgot your birthday 🙇” shows more remorse than 😬, and “you saved my life today 🙇” shows more gratitude than 🙏. It also frames requests humbly: “could you possibly cover for me 🙇.” The size of the gesture should match the size of the favor or the mistake.

A playful fourth meaning is worship. Fans use 🙇 to bow down before a performance, a recipe or a friend’s good decision, in the spirit of “we’re not worthy.” That overlaps with the kneeling emoji but keeps a lighter tone. The exaggeration is the point; nobody is literally prostrating themselves over a guitar solo. Context separates this from a real apology easily, since praise usually follows.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Use it when a plain “sorry” feels too small: running very late, cancelling plans, forgetting something important. It adds visible humility. For favors, it softens the ask and shows you know you are imposing. Friends also send it after receiving help that went well beyond the expected, as a deep thank-you.

contexts.label: Around the world
contexts.body: In Japan and among people who message in Japanese, 🙇 is routine and tied to politeness formulas used with colleagues, customers and elders. Bowing is also part of etiquette in Korea and other East Asian cultures, so the meaning is readily understood there. Western users are split between the correct reading and the “head on desk” interpretation.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: With Japanese clients or coworkers, the emoji fits naturally into apologies for delays and thanks for cooperation. In other workplaces it is less familiar and may puzzle recipients, though “so sorry for the late reply 🙇” is usually understood. It reads as earnest, so it suits real apologies better than trivial ones.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Fans post 🙇 under performances and artwork to say they bow to the creator’s talent. Students use it for studying fatigue, picturing a head dropped onto a desk. In fan communities around anime and Japanese pop culture, it keeps its original sense of respectful thanks or apology. The same emoji can therefore mean reverence in one comment and burnout in the next.

examples.text: I’m so sorry I missed your call, my phone died 🙇
examples.meaning: A sincere apology that goes beyond a casual “sorry.”

examples.text: Thank you for staying late to help me finish 🙇
examples.meaning: Deep gratitude toward someone who made a real effort.

examples.text: Could you please water my plants while I’m away? 🙇

examples.meaning: Bowing down in admiration of someone’s skill.
Head-on-desk exhaustion, the common misreading used on purpose.

examples.text: Please forgive me, I ate your leftovers 🙇‍♂️
examples.meaning: A dramatic, half-joking plea for forgiveness.

combos.meaning: An earnest plea or very deep thanks.
A flustered, anxious apology, a pairing common in Japanese messaging.
Bowing to royalty; acknowledging someone as the best.
Begging desperately or apologizing with great drama.

confusedWith.difference: 🙏 shows pressed palms for please, thanks or prayer. 🙇 uses the whole body, which makes the apology or request feel deeper and more formal, closer to throwing yourself on someone’s mercy.
🧎 is a figure upright on its knees, used for begging, worship jokes and proposals. 🙇 is specifically a bow with the head lowered, rooted in Japanese apology and gratitude.
💆 shows hands on a person’s head during a massage. People sometimes think 🙇 is lying on a massage table, but it depicts a bow and has nothing to do with relaxation.

avoid: Do not use it sarcastically toward someone expecting a real apology, since mock-bowing can inflame things.
Avoid assuming everyone knows it is a bow; add words if the apology or thanks matters.
Skip it for trivial slips in formal Japanese business contexts, where over-apologizing can seem insincere.
design: The emoji shows the head and shoulders of a person facing the viewer and bent forward, with a flat surface or hands in front suggesting the floor. Several platforms add small lines or triangles above the head to indicate the bowing motion. It has gender-neutral, woman 🙇‍♀️ and man 🙇‍♂️ forms, each with skin tones.

faqs.a: No. It looks that way to many people because only the head, shoulders and a flat line are visible, but the emoji depicts a deep bow. It represents apology, gratitude or a humble request in Japanese culture, not exercise.

faqs.q: What does 🙇‍♀️ or 🙇‍♂️ mean from someone?
faqs.a: They are apologizing sincerely, thanking you deeply or asking for a favor. If neither fits, they may be using the popular alternative reading of being tired or overwhelmed, head down on a desk. The rest of the message will show which.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🙇 and 🙏?
faqs.a: Both can say please, thank you or sorry. 🙏 is a general-purpose gesture used worldwide. 🙇 is a full bow, so it conveys greater humility and is the more formal choice in Japanese etiquette. Use it when you want to show you really mean it.

faqs.q: What does dogeza have to do with this emoji?
faqs.a: Dogeza is the Japanese practice of kneeling and bowing until the head nears the floor, used for the gravest apologies or requests. Many designs of 🙇 resemble it, which is why the emoji carries such strong associations with begging forgiveness.
